Report_ID: All-cause mortality (total deaths from any cause)
Title: Principal Results of the Japanese Trial to Assess Optimal Systolic Blood Pressure in Elderly Hypertensive Patients (JATOS)
Author: JATOS Study Group
Comment: Paper reports only event counts and a chi-square p-value; no risk ratio, odds ratio or confidence interval for all-cause mortality was reported, so no ratio effect measure was recorded. Arm ordering follows the synthesis plan (higher/mild target as group_1 = treatment), which is the reverse of the paper's own table ordering.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Mild treatment (higher BP target: systolic <160 but ≥140 mmHg; achieved 145.6/78.1 mmHg)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Outpatients aged 65–85 years with essential hypertension and pretreatment systolic BP ≥160 mmHg
Recruitment source: Japanese outpatient clinics (Japan Physicians Association / Japanese Society of Hypertension network), registered April 2001–December 2002
Outcome measurement: Number of patients who died of any cause during the 2-year treatment period, out of total randomized per arm (intention to treat)
Outcome variable: All-cause mortality (total deaths from any cause)
effect_direction: Fewer deaths in the higher-target (mild treatment) arm: 42/2206 (1.9%) vs 54/2212 (2.4%) in the lower-target (strict) arm; RR ≈ 0.78, favouring the higher target, not statistically significant (p=0.22).

Title: Effects of Intensive Antihypertensive Treatment on Chinese Hypertensive Patients Older Than 70 Years
Author: Wei Y, Jin Z, Shen G, Zhao X, Yang W, Zhong Y, Wang J
Comment: Arm labelling follows the synthesis plan: the paper's 'standard' (<150/90) arm is recorded as the treatment/higher-target arm (group_1) and the 'intensive' (<140/90) arm as the control/lower-target arm (group_2). The paper itself lists intensive first in Table V. No risk ratio was reported by the paper; only counts, percentages and a chi-square P value (.001).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Higher BP target arm: standard treatment, target BP <150/90 mm Hg (achieved 149.7/82.1 mm Hg)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Chinese hypertensive patients older than 70 years (mean age 76.6 y), outpatient general practice care
Recruitment source: Outpatient clinic, Songjiang Branch to Shanghai First People's Hospital, Shanghai, China
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of total deaths per randomized arm, Table V
effect_direction: More deaths in the higher-target (standard, <150/90) arm: 87/361 (24.1%) vs 51/363 (14.0%) in the lower-target (intensive, <140/90) arm; RR ≈ 1.72, favouring the lower target (p=0.001).

Title: Trial of Intensive Blood-Pressure Control in Older Patients with Hypertension (STEP trial)
Author: Zhang W, Zhang S, Deng Y, et al. (STEP Study Group)
Comment: The paper reports a hazard ratio of 1.11 (95% CI 0.78–1.56) for death from any cause, but it is oriented as INTENSIVE (lower target) vs STANDARD (higher target) — i.e. the reverse of the synthesis plan's framing, in which the higher/standard target arm is the treatment arm. The HR field was therefore left empty to avoid direction reversal downstream; pool from the raw counts (higher-target/standard arm = 64/4268; lower-target/intensive arm = 67/4243). Note also that this trial's absolute targets (130 to <150 vs 110 to <130 mm Hg systolic) are lower than the plan's nominal 150-160/95-100 vs 140/90 mm Hg, though the standard arm is the trial's own less intensively treated (higher-target) group. Trial stopped early for cardiovascular benefit; no multiplicity adjustment for secondary outcomes.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Higher BP target arm: standard treatment, systolic target 130 to <150 mm Hg') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Patients 60 to 80 years of age with hypertension (Han Chinese), without history of stroke
Recruitment source: 42 clinical centers throughout China, recruited January 10 to December 31, 2017
Outcome measurement: Number and percentage of patients who died from any cause per randomized arm
effect_direction: Near-null, marginally fewer deaths in the higher-target (standard, 130–<150) arm: 64/4268 (1.5%) vs 67/4243 (1.6%) in the lower-target (intensive, 110–<130) arm; RR ≈ 0.95, essentially no difference.

Title: Target Blood Pressure for Treatment of Isolated Systolic Hypertension in the Elderly: Valsartan in Elderly Isolated Systolic Hypertension (VALISH) Study
Author: Ogihara et al.
Comment: The paper's reported adjusted hazard ratio 0.78 (95% CI 0.46-1.33) is oriented as STRICT (lower target) vs MODERATE (higher target), i.e. the inverse of the synthesis plan's treatment/control framing; it was therefore not entered into the hazard_ratio field to avoid mis-oriented pooling. Event counts and per-arm Ns are entered with the higher-target (moderate) arm as group_1/treatment. Denominators 1545/1534 are the ITT analysed populations (3260 randomized, 181 lost to follow-up).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Moderate blood pressure control group (higher target, systolic BP 140-150 mm Hg; less intensively treated arm)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: randomized controlled trial (PROBE, open-label, blinded end point)
Participant type: Elderly patients aged 70-84 years with isolated systolic hypertension (sitting systolic BP 160-199 mm Hg, diastolic BP <90 mm Hg)
Recruitment source: 461 centers in Japan, registered February 2004 to August 2005
Outcome measurement: Number of deaths from any cause / number of patients in each target BP arm (intention-to-treat)
effect_direction: More deaths in the higher-target (moderate control, 140–150) arm: 30/1534 (1.96%) vs 24/1545 (1.55%) in the lower-target (strict, <140) arm; RR ≈ 1.26, favouring the lower target, not statistically significant (p=0.362).
